subject: DESIGN: Cloud Master project 1 of 3 -- 'Build a Cloud Auditor'. Student inherits a cloud account wasting quota; they build a tool that inventories the tenant and finds orphans (volume attached to nothing, security group on no server, network with no ports, snapshot whose parent is gone). 4 phases: enumerate -> classify (student writes the rules) -> report -> prove it against a server-side seed they cannot inspect. Fits every measured constraint: no data-plane route needed (#250), read-mostly so it does not fight CLI concurrency (#248), single-instance, and the load-bearing check reads live cloud state through the bridge rather than a file in the student's container (BUG-077 lesson applied at design time). NOT COVERED by any of the six labs. Nancy dispatched for design review BEFORE any build -- the two things I most want killed are (a) whether a student can hand-write a passing report without building a tool, which would make this grade 'did you notice' not 'did you build', and (b) whether seeding into a PERSISTENT tenant is fundamentally wrong given #249.
description:
Design under review 2026-08-01
[2026-08-01 04:14] NANCY KILLED v1 (design review, before any build -- the process working). Two STRUCTURAL failures, not tunable:
(1) GRADING A REPORT CANNOT CERTIFY A TOOL. The check layer only ever sees the findings file, never the code. Diffing report claims against live state proves the REPORT IS ACCURATE, not that a program produced it. A student can eyeball 5-15 resources in a quota-capped tenant and hand-type a matching report. Unlike the capstone -- where checks 26/27 carry the thesis independently of the forgeable 25/28 -- EVERY phase output here is a file, so there is no backstop check anywhere that can only pass if a tool exists.
(2) 'INVENT ONE AND IT FAILS' WOULD PUNISH CORRECT STUDENTS. The six labs leave ORGANIC orphans in the persistent tenant: the 1-instance quota forces server deletion, and nothing in any lab tears down web-sg (secgroup) or lab5-net + its router (neutron) afterwards. A student whose tool is 100% correct reports those too -- correctly -- and my rule marks it wrong.
Also: all four orphan classes are the boolean negation of existing checks (20, 23, 24, 6, 12), so the only NEW content is the packaging -- which is precisely the part v1 could not grade.
REVISION SENT: the grader RUNS the student's tool. Mutate the tenant AFTER their last edit, exec their executable, compute ground truth server-side at that instant from /verify, pass = output matches. Closes (1) because a static hand-written report cannot track a mutation made after it was written. Closes (2) because ground truth is COMPUTED not seeded, so an organically-orphaned web-sg is genuinely orphaned and reporting it is correct. Closes the BUG-077 staleness shape because NOTHING is persisted -- mutate, run, compare, discard.
Open for Nancy: container-side exec poisoning (#252), CLI concurrency (#248) making grading unreliable for honest students, whether create-only mutation suffices, and the output-contract line between gradeable and writing the program for them.
[2026-08-01 04:14] BACKLOG RECONCILED (owed to Nancy): no collision with #247. The 8 designed Stage 4 labs are Cinder, Read the Wall (quota exhaustion, HELD), Rescue the Data, security groups, launch chain, Neutron self-service, Keystone reduced-privilege, Horizon-vs-CLI. NONE is an audit/orphan/cleanup lab -- every orphan|audit|cleanup|leftover hit in openstack-sandbox-scoping.md is infrastructure-internal (session orphaning, credential deletion, quota negatives), not student content. The doc argues FOR this content at line 589 ('real cloud resources outlive your session and cleanup is part of the job') and never builds it. ONE ADJACENCY: held 'Read the Wall' is quota exhaustion -- different question (why can't I create vs what is rotting) but a near neighbour; re-check framing if it is ever unblocked.
[2026-08-01 04:23] DESIGN STATUS: NOT BUILDABLE YET, and the blocker is now measured rather than suspected. #248 is CPU-bound (container pinned at its cpus:0.5 cap; memory peaked 61%, no OOM), and one openstack call costs 4.8s SOLO. A tool covering four resource classes needs 5+ calls = ~24s with zero contention. That questions whether exec-the-student's-CLI-tool is viable in this container at all, which is a design-level question, not a timeout-tuning one.
Nancy's three edges from the latest round are answered and folded in: the per-session grading lock carries its OWN TTL so a hung exec cannot permanently lock a session; probes are matched by server-recorded ID not by name pattern (BUG-056 lesson -- otherwise a student could name a resource audit-probe-<their-sessionId>-1 and hide a real orphan from ground truth); and the age-based sweep threshold derives from the measured worst case rather than being picked.
NEXT DECISION, needs the operator or Nancy: keep it CLI-based and raise cpus, or teach raw REST instead. REST is faster AND arguably better content (authenticate, call the API directly) but it is a materially different project from the one reviewed.

notes.text:
TOOLING DECISION RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT (operator still owns the final call): openstacksdk, one process. 2,321 ms vs 19,363 ms for the CLI, overrides confirmed working, 5/5 calls returning real data, and ZERO new prerequisites since the SDK reads the same clouds.yaml every lab already uses. Raw REST is faster again (816 ms) but teaches token auth from zero, which none of the six labs scaffold.
NANCY'S REMAINING TWO, both accepted and NOT closed:
  (a) CONCURRENCY of the new workload is UNMEASURED. The 4-concurrent test must be rerun against the chosen option before the timeout and lock-TTL numbers are trusted -- those were derived from the CLI-spawn shape that is being replaced.
  (b) 'CONNECT ONCE' MUST BE AN EXPLICIT TAUGHT CONSTRAINT on the page, not an implicit trap. Five labs conditioned students to run one-shot CLI commands, so 'shell out five times in a script' is the MEDIAN first attempt. A student with perfect classification logic would time out for a reason unrelated to whether they understood orphans. State it as a learning objective WITH the why: connecting is expensive, and reconnecting in a loop is the most common way people make cloud tooling slow.

ALL DESIGN GATES CLOSED 2026-08-01. Six rounds of Nancy; the structural mechanism was never killed after the v1 rewrite. Final measured position:
  CONCURRENCY (the last gate): SDK solo 2,504 ms; SDK x4 concurrent 10,184 ms, CPU ~50% (cap), MEM 112/384 MiB. Stronger than like-for-like -- the CLI test was 4 concurrent x ONE call (24,303 ms, 4 calls total) while this is 4 concurrent x FIVE calls (10,184 ms, 20 calls total). ~12x throughput. Four students running full audits at once finish in ten seconds. The earlier lock-TTL/timeout reasoning was built on 19.5s-and-climbing and should be rebuilt on these.
  SINGLE-SAMPLE RISK: closed structurally, not by sampling more. personalCloudsYaml() at server.js:47-65 is ONE TEMPLATE; the only per-slot variance is cred_id and cred_secret. auth_url, region, interface and all five endpoint overrides are hardcoded literals identical across all 30 slots. If that function ever grows a conditional, this assumption dies with it.
  SPEC CORRECTION (Nancy): 'zero new concepts' was an overclaim. AUTH is free (same clouds.yaml, same credential). The LIBRARY is not -- conn.block_storage.volumes() is a Python object/generator API and six labs taught only `openstack ... -f value -c X` table output. Phase 1 must teach connect + iterate a collection, and the page should say so plainly.
AWAITING OPERATOR: SDK vs raw REST. Recommendation SDK (2,321 ms, no new auth concepts) over REST (816 ms, teaches token auth from zero). The concurrency numbers remove any speed argument for REST.
